commit.message:
Revoke refresh sessions on staff role changes (#307)

* Revoke sessions atomically with staff role changes

* Test role-change session revocation

* Expose refresh token to security integration tests

* Prove role changes revoke refresh tokens

* Track role target only for atomic stamp rotation

fix(auth): revoke sessions on user admin actions

A missing login_sessions row is 'not_found' and authRequired lets it
through, so DELETE-ing rows never revoked anything: old JWTs stayed
valid after password reset/change, role change, user delete and logout,
and terminals already open kept running (proxies check revoked at
connect time only).

- add revokeUserSessions(): UPDATE revoked=1 (never DELETE), then
  closeSessionConnections() (4001) on every revoked session
- revoke on user delete, real role change, admin reset, own password
  change; close open sockets on logout
- authRequired rejects tokens whose user no longer exists, so the FK
  cascade (login_sessions gone with the user) cannot reopen the hole
- PUT /users/:id rejects changing your own role (400), like the UI and
  DELETE; the JWT would keep the old role until expiry
- unref module-level cleanup timers (profile, auth, wsTicket, oidc) so
  tests importing those routers can exit
- tests: 8 cases, each fails without its fix

- src/lib/auth.ts: loadSession (checks revoked/expired/active), requireAuth,

feat(iam): per-role Revoke sessions (revokeSessionsBefore) — #147

The AWS AWSRevokeOlderSessions analog on kind: Role. Split from #136 §1;
ships the recommended per-role cutoff (path 2), not a per-session deny-list.

- awssts: the sealed session token now carries its issue time (iat); the seal
  stays stateless.
- Role XRD: spec.revokeSessionsBefore (RFC3339). The aws-shim verify path
  (after SigV4) falls closed when a session's iat precedes the role's cutoff;
  new assumes survive. Cuts one role's sessions without a global key rotation.
- roleCutoffCache: reads the cutoff off the Role claim via the same dynamic
  client + RBAC the trust resolver already uses (one source of truth, no
  composition change, no new RBAC). Short TTL; serves last-known on a read blip
  so a control-plane hiccup neither un-revokes nor denies all.
- BFF POST /api/iam/roles/{name}/revoke-sessions (server-generated now cutoff,
  gated on update-roles) + revokeSessionsBefore on the role view.
- Console: the Role → Revoke sessions tab, was a disabled "Part B" placeholder,
  is now a live confirm-gated action showing the current cutoff.
- docs/aws-shim.md: revocation levers rewritten (TTL / per-role / key rotation);
  single-session revoke stays an honest not-built edge.

Tests: awssts iat roundtrip; shim revoke path (before/after cutoff, nil/no
cutoff) + roleCutoffCache parse/absence/failure-posture; BFF view. OpenAPI
regenerated. No terraform-provider change (Role is not a provider kind).

BUILT + gates green; NOT deployed, NOT live-verified, console UX unverified.

commit.message:
feat(auth): OWNER/ADMIN/STAFF roles, account administration API, owner recovery key

- Migration 0011 (forward-only): rebuild staff_accounts with the three
  roles and must_change_password (sessions end once, as the rebuild
  requires), owner_recovery_keys holding SHA-256 verifiers only, a shared
  auth_throttle table, and audit/session indexes.
- src/accounts.ts: server-enforced rules. ADMIN manages STAFF only; OWNER
  manages everyone; the last active OWNER cannot be disabled or demoted;
  password, username, role and disable changes revoke sessions; accounts
  given a password by someone else must change it before anything else.
- Self service: change own username, display name and password; revoke
  other sessions. Owners rotate or revoke a single-use recovery key.
- /api/recovery/owner can only reset the key owner's password, re-enable
  it, revoke its sessions and consume the key; throttled per client.
- Login throttling moves from per-isolate memory to D1.
- Every account/recovery change is audited with safe metadata only.
- 19 new tests cover roles, sessions, recovery, throttling, cross-site
  requests, secret hygiene and migrating a database already in use.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01VB55pF1Dxh72UKtvZag2XX

fix!: revoke JWTs and role sessions when permissions are withdrawn

- tibba-cache: add RedisCache::mget and shared credential revocation
  markers (revoke_user_credentials / revoke_role_credentials /
  is_credential_revoked), checked with a single MGET
- tibba-session: revocation now uses the shared markers and also covers
  the session's roles; add revoke_role_sessions
- tibba-jwt: JwtUser rejects access tokens issued before a user/role
  revocation; requires init_revocation_cache (fail-closed 503 otherwise)
- router-user: refresh tokens record their issue time and are refused
  after the user's credentials are revoked (legacy entries fail safe)
- tibba-model-builtin: PermissionModel::soft_delete_by_code returns the
  roles that lost the permission
- tibba-rbac: add RbacAdmin (grant / revoke / delete_permission) that
  revokes affected roles' credentials after withdrawing permissions
- app: wire the JWT revocation cache at startup; reject jwt access/refresh
  TTL longer than session TTL

BREAKING CHANGE: tibba_jwt::init_revocation_cache must be called before
JwtUser is used; soft_delete_by_code returns Vec<String>; refresh token
records changed format.

Merge pull request #138 from G0kul17/fix/revoke-sessions-on-role-change

Revoke sessions when an admin changes a user's role

fix(auth): unified principal store — OIDC issuer+sub identity, revocable SSO and local sessions (A02, A08/A04 residuals)

Adapts teploy-observe f631c81 (migration 040 unified principals) to dash's
users.json store: every identity that can hold a session is a persisted
principal row whose AuthEpoch sessions embed at issuance and every request
revalidates unconditionally — local accounts and external identities alike.

- A02: sessions carry the principal key (sub) + epoch. Local issuance
  already captured the epoch inside authenticate's locked read; OIDC
  issuance now captures it inside upsertOIDCPrincipal's persist-then-publish
  critical section, so a revocation landing between verification and
  issuance leaves the new session immediately dead. A missing row (deleted
  account, revoked principal, pre-principal session) is a dead session.
- A08 residual / pass-7 A04 residual: OIDC identity is the issuer-namespaced
  subject oidc:<sha256(issuer)[:16]>:<sub>, not display-name claims. First
  sign-in creates the principal; later ones refresh username/email/role (IdP
  authoritative) while preserving the epoch so one device's sign-in does not
  retire another's session — and live-role reads propagate IdP role changes
  to existing sessions without killing them.
- New admin surface: POST /api/users/{u}/revoke-sessions (local) and
  GET /api/sso + POST /api/sso/revoke (principals), both admin-gated.
- Additive migration: users.json gains an optional oidc_principals list;
  pre-principal installs load with an empty set (in-memory sessions die at
  restart as before), duplicate subjects fail closed as an auth outage.
  Role change revokes via the existing epoch bump (now gate-tested).

Acceptance gates in principals_test.go: issue -> revoke -> old token
rejected (local + OIDC), role change revokes, issuer scoping, display-name
non-collision, missing-row death, store round-trip, and a concurrent
login/revoke/request race test (run under -race).

fix(security): revoke sessions on tenant-membership role change / removal

The only cross-feature session-revoke hook fired on passwordHash change
only — a member demoted or removed from a tenant kept a valid JWT until
the 30-day TTL. update-member-roles now revokes every session of that
user (a role change is security-relevant everywhere, not just in this
tenant); remove-member revokes only that tenant's sessions, leaving a
multi-tenant user logged in elsewhere. Both call the existing
revoke-all-for-user handler via a soft (registry-checked) cross-feature
call, since tenant must still boot without sessions mounted. The
postSave hook itself now also fires on `status` changes, not just
passwordHash.

commit.message:
feat(identity): browser sessions, RBAC admin API and role CLI for Phase 7

- Refresh token can travel as an httpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie when
  the client opts in with X-Refresh-Token-Transport: cookie (ADR-0006).
- Access tokens carry a sid claim; sessions record user agent, IP and
  last use. GET/DELETE /api/v1/users/me/sessions list and revoke them.
- /api/v1/users/me returns the caller's roles.
- /api/v1/admin/users: SUPPORT and ADMIN can search and view users;
  only ADMIN can change status. A non-ACTIVE status revokes every
  session in the same transaction, and refresh rejects tokens whose
  owner is no longer ACTIVE.
- python -m app.cli grant-role|revoke-role bootstraps staff accounts;
  no HTTP endpoint grants roles.

Revoke a user's sessions when an admin changes their role

The role is copied into the session at sign-in and every guard reads it
from there, so a demoted admin stayed an admin, and a promoted user stayed
a user, until their session idled out. Any role change now revokes the
target's sessions the same way disabling does, and the audit row records
how many were revoked.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(api): demotion and admin revoke-all-sessions revoke API keys (RFC-82 R3)

Removing the admin system role through setUserRoles revokes every active
key of the user in the same transaction (reason admin_role_removed), so a
later grant revives none (review 2, I1); an administrator revoking all of
a user's sessions does the same (reason sessions_revoked, I2).
Hardening: logout-all and admin revoke-all commit the database before the
Redis sessions go (m1); createApiKey re-reads the user row under lock and
refuses a suspended user or a changed password (m2); revokeApiKey locks
the users row first, matching suspendUser's lock order (m3).
RFC-82 R3, RFC-31 R6, RFC-50 R5/R9, RFC-41 row (m4), spec, CLAUDE.md
(users.delete, m6).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01PC93e8ZuvRNV2Enn9jjW4y

fix(user): revoke sessions on role change, not only on block

Role is embedded in the JWT and never re-derived per request, so demoting a
user's role (e.g. an admin demoted after a security incident) left their
existing access token acting under the old role for up to its remaining
lifetime — only a BLOCKED status change triggered session revocation.

Revoke all sessions whenever the role actually changes too.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(security): invalidate sessions on account changes; replace Redis KEYS with SCAN

- LoginSessionManager: single entry point for session writes, keeps a
  login_user_tokens:{userId} index so sessions can be revoked/refreshed:
  * admin/forgot-password reset -> all sessions revoked
  * own password change -> other sessions revoked, current kept
  * disable/delete user -> revoked; role/dept/menu change -> permissions reloaded
  Actions run after transaction commit.
- Redis KEYS -> SCAN (online users, cache monitor); SystemTask uses DBSIZE;
  online user list uses MGET + one dept query instead of N+1.
- Clearing all cache no longer wipes sessions, login retry counters,
  captchas, reset-password tokens or SSO state.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message: Revoke login and consent sessions when user is deactivated, and consent sessions when role of user has changed

feat: team access management — roles, member removal, invite revoke, device sessions (#30)

* feat(api,hq): team access management — roles, removal, invite revoke, device sessions

The session row's role is authoritative at request time (tenant.ts), so
every role change re-stamps the member's live sessions inside the same
transaction as the membership write — a demoted admin loses their powers
on the next request, not the next login.

api: PATCH /api/team/members/:userId accepts {skills?, role?}; DELETE
removes the membership (never the global User row) and revokes the
member's sessions; POST /members/:userId/sign-out is the lost-phone
button; GET /api/team/invites lists pending invites (never tokenHash);
POST /invites/:id/revoke kills one; GET/DELETE /api/auth/sessions is the
caller's own device list with self-scoped revoke. Owner boundaries,
self-edit and last-owner guards throughout, audited.

hq: the Crews module becomes the management surface — per-row role
select, two-step remove confirm, sign-out-all-devices, pending-invites
panel with revoke, and a your-devices panel whose current-session revoke
redirects to /login. ROLE_OPTIONS lifted to a shared module.

* fix(api,hq): close last-owner TOCTOU race, self sign-out guard, expired-invite 404

The pre-transaction owner count in PATCH/DELETE /members/:userId raced:
two concurrent demote/remove requests both observe two owners and both
commit, leaving zero — unrecoverable without DB surgery. The authoritative
check now runs inside the transaction behind a per-org advisory lock
(hashtext('org-owners:' || orgId), namespaced away from the technician
assignment locks), re-reading the membership and re-counting owners
there; the outer checks stay as the fast path for friendly errors.
Discriminated tx results surface the same 409/404 bodies.

The self-row 'Sign out all devices' now disables with a title pointing at
the Your devices panel — it revoked the operator's own live session and
left a dead console. And revoking an already-expired invite 404s like
the message says, matching the list filter.

---------

commit.message:
feat(PLA-0010/00367): revoke active sessions on role change

Role updates went through users.Service.Update via a single
pool.Exec — when a target's role changed, their existing session
rows kept revoked=FALSE, so a downgraded user could continue using
their old elevated token until expiry. R035 flagged this as a real
escalation window, especially for gadmin→user demotions.

Implementation choice: reuse the existing sessions.revoked column
rather than introducing a new generation counter. Three other call
sites in auth/service.go (token-reuse detection, password change,
forced reset) already do `UPDATE sessions SET revoked = TRUE WHERE
user_id = $1`; the auth middleware already treats revoked sessions
as 401. This keeps the revocation surface uniform.

Changes:
  - users.Service.Update wraps the user UPDATE + sessions revoke in
    a single pgx tx so a partial failure cannot leave the role
    advanced with sessions intact.
  - Detect role-change strictly: in.Role != nil AND new role differs
    from the targetRole loaded for ceiling checks. Same-role no-op
    does NOT nuke sessions.
  - Emit a separate `user.role_changed` audit entry with metadata
    {from, to} alongside the existing `user.updated` row, so
    security review can spot escalations without inferring from a
    raw users.role_id diff.

Tests (integration against dev tunnel):
  - TestUpdate_RoleChange_RevokesSessions       — gadmin→padmin nukes
  - TestUpdate_NoRoleChange_DoesNotRevokeSessions — IsActive flip safe
  - TestUpdate_SameRole_DoesNotRevokeSessions   — defensive no-op

Note: original story description suggested a `user_sessions.generation`
counter and a `PUT /api/users/:id/role` endpoint. The actual code path
is `PATCH /api/users/:id` (handler.go line ~135) routed through
Service.Update, and the existing sessions table already supports the
revoke pattern. Fix uses the canonical surface — same security
outcome with less new schema.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
